title: Norway May Restrict Online Games for Under-16s
paragraphs: Many children spend hours on social media, playing online games and chatting with friends. But in Norway, some of these activities could soon be banned for children under 16.

The government is planning new rules to protect children from dangers it sees online. And the rules could affect more apps and games than first planned, with platforms such as TikTok, Snapchat and even Roblox potentially affected.
Roblox is an online gaming platform where people can create games, play them and talk to other users.

The government is worried about children seeing harmful content, spending too much time online and talking to strangers. It also wants to stop companies from showing children certain types of advertising.
At first, Norway planned to leave online games and messaging apps out of the ban. But now, it wants to look at how each platform might affect children's safety.
However, the proposed ban wouldn't apply to every app. For example, messaging apps that children use to communicate with their schools may still be allowed.
Under the proposed law, technology companies would have to check users' ages to make sure children under 16 couldn't access restricted platforms.
The proposed new law is to be submitted to parliament before the end of 2026.
Norway isn't the only European country taking steps to protect children online.
Denmark has already introduced rules banning children under 15 from social media, while Spain is working on a social media ban for children under 16.
France also tried to introduce a social media ban for children under 15. But it was blocked by the Constitutional Council, the country's top court, because of concerns about freedom of speech.
The European Union is also looking at new restrictions for social media, online games, video platforms and other internet services for young people.
For now, Norway's plans are still being discussed. But if they become law, they could change the way the country's young people spend their time online.
